redbook.body: We offer a 150-year-old dialogue between nature and the senses. Our formulas use the exact high-quality Thai botanicals recorded in the legendary Red Book, optimized to restore your balance today. From the old streets of Songkhla to your pocket.

c1.title: The Book That Survived.
c1.body: A leather-bound ledger of remedies, carried out of Old Songkhla and kept in the family for five generations. Water, war and time took almost everything else.

c2.title: Written to Be Read.
c2.body: Its pages are not incantations. They are measurements — grams, hours, the exact hour of the day to pick each flower. A working manual, kept by someone who expected it to be used.

c3.title: Still in Use.
c3.body: Every formula we make traces to a numbered recipe in that book. We have modernised the vessel, never the proportions.

c1.headline: 150 Years in the Shadows.
c1.body: It began with a single, crimson-bound volume. A 19th-century medical journal belonging to Khun Apiban Bo Plup (APB), a sanitation officer during the transformative reign of King Rama V. Within its weathered pages lay a forgotten dialogue between nature and the human spirit—a collection of botanical rituals used to maintain the balance of life.
c1.alt: A page from the Red Book — weathered manuscript paper with handwritten Thai herbal recipes

c2.headline: The Visionary of Old Songkhla.
c2.body: Khun Apiban Bo Plup was more than a practitioner; he was a guardian of wellness in an era of change. As a public health pioneer in Old Town Songkhla, he understood that true restoration comes from the harmony of the senses. His “Red Book” was not just a record of herbs, but a map to self-healing—a practice where one takes the power of well-being into their own hands.
c2.alt: Painted portrait of Khun Apiban Bo Plup, seated in Rama V-era dress

c3.headline: Ancient Wisdom for the Modern Soul.
c3.body: In the 19th century, self-care was an intuitive ritual. Today, we bring that intuition back. We believe that the modern fast-paced world needs the slow, deliberate magic of ancestral Thai botanicals. Our philosophy is simple: Modern Rituals rooted in Ancient Truths. We provide the tools; you perform the ritual.
c3.alt: Thai herbs being ground in a stone mortar

c4.headline: A Legacy Reborn Through Family.
c4.body: APB is not a solo journey. It is a collaborative revival by the descendants of the Songkhla family. Uniting multiple households, we have come together to breathe life into our ancestor's archives. Each bottle is a testament to our family's shared commitment to preserving our artisanal heritage and sharing it with a global generation.

recipe1.title: The 1870 Botanical Inhaler formula
recipe1.body: A precise combination of Camphor, Borneol, Peppermint oil, and 14 sun-dried roots and blossoms. Preserved in a traditional unglazed clay pot to maintain proper ambient humidity.

rows.label: Menthol (เกล็ดสะระแหน่)
14 Sun-Dried Herbs (สมุนไพร 14 ชนิด)

recipe1.note: Dry the blossoms for three noon phases until they release their light soul. Blend with oil in unglazed clay.
recipe1.imageAlt: Original Red Book pages showing handwritten ingredient columns ruled in red ink

recipe2.title: The Restoration Oil recipe (Phetmongkol)
recipe2.body: Formulated to ground the senses. Slowly infused cold-pressed coconut oil, plai root, lemongrass stalks, and fresh kaffir lime zest, aged under shelter for thirty-three days.

rows.label: Lemongrass Stalks (ตะไคร้หอม)
Fresh Kaffir Lime Zest (ผิวมะกรูด)
Plai Root (เหง้าไพล)
Cold-Pressed Coconut Oil (น้ำมันมะพร้าว)

recipe2.note: Age the infusion under shelter for thirty-three days to allow the earth properties to stabilize.
recipe2.imageAlt: The red cloth-bound manuscript on a workbench beside citrus fruit and an unglazed clay pot

recipe3.title: Tenets of the Guardian's Craft
recipe3.body: Tenet I: No synthetic enhancers shall be introduced. Tenet II: All botanicals are gathered in accordance with lunar cycles. Tenet III: Scent is the bridge between cognitive balance and raw physical comfort.
recipe3.note: The breath is the first gate of wellness. Cleanse it, and the spirit shall follow.
recipe3.imageAlt: The Red Book preserved under a glass case with dried botanicals and a stone mortar
